contexts.paragraph_text: For deterministic preprocessing shared by training and serving, parity tests compare transformed features for the same raw record under the released code and state. The tests declare a numerical tolerance where execution backends differ.
The missing requests are the source of the distortion. Figure 2 aligns the two arrival policies against one server pause so that the change in offered work remains visible.

Offline batch processing eliminates arrival scheduling entirely; the harness pre-stages large input batches in memory to saturate accelerator execution units, maximize memory bandwidth utilization, and measure peak sustained throughput.

Serving runtimes such as vLLM23 and TensorRT-LLM improve throughput via two mechanisms: reclaiming wasted compute from completed sequences and shortening queue wait times for new arrivals (Kwon et al. 2023; NVIDIA 2026f). However, admitting new requests dynamically creates a systems collision between prompt prefill and token decoding. Long-prompt prefill often exposes high arithmetic intensity and can occupy the GPU for tens of milliseconds. Low-batch decoding often has less weight reuse and is memory-bandwidth bound, advancing one token per active sequence at a time. When an engine admits an entire long prompt before advancing active decodes, those streams wait for that prefill, stretching their inter-token gaps. Sarathi-Serve resolves this interference through chunked prefill and stall-free batching (Agrawal et al. 2024). By splitting long prompts into fixed-size chunks (e.g., 512 tokens) and co-scheduling a single chunk alongside active decode requests per step, the scheduler limits the prefill work admitted per iteration, reducing interference with active decodes. Measured iteration times determine the resulting token cadence.

PagedAttention,25 introduced in vLLM, resolves this fragmentation by applying operating system virtual memory paging to accelerator memory (Kwon et al. 2023). In static contiguous allocation, reserving maximum sequence length memory up front causes internal waste, while freed regions may be too small or poorly placed to satisfy a new contiguous reservation. Instead of allocating one contiguous region per sequence, PagedAttention divides the KV cache into fixed-size blocks mapped through a block table. A sequence’s cache can therefore occupy noncontiguous physical blocks. When a sequence completes, its blocks return to a free pool for reuse. Rather than copying noncontiguous blocks into a temporary contiguous buffer before computing attention, a specialized PagedAttention CUDA kernel traverses the block table directly, staging noncontiguous blocks into on-chip SRAM during query-key multiplication. By eliminating external fragmentation and bounding internal waste to each sequence’s last, partially filled block, PagedAttention reduced KV-cache waste below 4 percent in the reported evaluation and enabled substantially higher batch concurrency on the same accelerator hardware (Kwon et al. 2023). Paging decides where cache blocks live, however. It does not reduce the KV bytes stored per token; a sequence needs another block only when its current allocation fills.

Attestation and key management add coordination work when admission or recovery requires renewed evidence and key delivery. The policy must specify when evidence expires and which changes require another check. Key rotation also needs a transition plan, while revocation after a suspected compromise may require interrupting work that no longer has valid authority. Hardware security modules can protect the keys used to authorize or wrap secrets, with node-level custody governed separately. When these operations delay participants or restart, their cost enters

This analytical budget charges each prompt token once at the prefill floor and reserves one decode floor step for each generated token. The first output token receives that allowance even though prefill supplies its initial logits. The budget therefore includes an extra decode-floor step relative to the measured post-TTFT interval, which contains only subsequent generation steps.

The copy path in figure 6 uses pinned host staging rather than the USB driver ring in the earlier baseline. The shared path separates physical storage from device mappings and marks the release that permits the capture engine to reuse that storage.
